title: Wh- Questions
subtitle: Who? What? Where? When? How? Why?
goals: I can ask with Who, What, Where, When, How and Why.
I can answer: a person, a thing, a place, a time, a way, a reason.
I can say how people move: over, under, around, through, up, down, across, past, into, out of, between.
I can name parts of my body: heart, lungs, brain, bones, muscles.
I can name sports and activities and say how they help my body.
I can bounce back when something is difficult.
teacherGoals: Question words ask for information: Who = person, What = thing, Where = place, When = time, How = way, Why = reason.
Word order: Wh- + am / is / are + subject + verb-ing. Who + is + verb-ing (no new order). Also Wh- + do / does + subject + verb.
Prepositions of movement with a verb: run around, climb through, jump over, go up / down, walk across, crawl under, jump into, step out of, run past, run between.
Reading words: heart, lungs, brain, bones, muscles, energy, relaxed, tired, strong, stretch, breathe, push, pull, exercise plan, short break.
Resilience: keep trying, learn from mistakes, stay positive, ask for help.
teacherNote: This week follows Compass Unit 2, pages 36–43: Sports and Activities (36), Wh- Questions (37), the reading about keeping the body strong (38–39), Prepositions of Movement (40), everyday ways to move (41), bouncing back (42) and the unit reflection (43). All sentences and the four short readings are written for this site; only the topic and target words come from the book.

learn.title: Six question words
learn.rule: Question words ask for information: **Who, What, Where, When, How, Why**.

practice.prompt: ___ is Leo running? — On the track.
practice.explain: On the track is a place → Where.

learn.teacherNote: Pupils can already answer yes / no questions. Question words ask for new information, so the answer is not Yes or No. Ask pupils to underline the question word first.

learn.title: Who? A person
learn.rule: **Who** asks about a person. Who + is + verb-ing …?

practice.explain: The answer is a person: Sam is.

learn.teacherNote: Who + is keeps the normal word order: Sam is running → Who is running? Even with two people we usually ask Who is …? The short answer changes: Sam is. / Sam and Leo are.

learn.title: What? A thing or an action
learn.rule: **What** asks about a thing. **What … doing?** asks about an action.

examples.a: They are having a short break.

practice.prompt: ___ is Leo pushing? — A big ball.
practice.explain: A big ball is a thing → What.

learn.teacherNote: Two common patterns: What is she passing? (a thing) and What is she doing? (an action; answer with the full verb).

learn.title: Where? A place
learn.rule: **Where** asks about a place. Where + is / are + who + verb-ing?

examples.label: A track is a path for running.

practice.prompt: ___ is Ana doing yoga? — In the garden.
practice.explain: In the garden is a place → Where.
Where → a place: down the slide.

learn.teacherNote: Is / are jumps before the subject: Leo is running → Where is Leo running? Short answers are fine and natural: On the track.

learn.title: When? A time
learn.rule: **When** asks about a time or a moment. When + do / does + who + verb?

practice.explain: After school is a time → When.

practice.prompt: When does Leo walk to school?

learn.teacherNote: When usually goes with habits, so we use do / does from Week 1. Link to the exercise plan: when can pupils move more?

learn.title: How? A way
learn.rule: **How** asks about a way or a manner.

examples.a: Tie your legs together. Then run!

practice.prompt: ___ is Ana pulling the wagon? — With a rope.
practice.explain: With a rope is a way → How.

learn.teacherNote: Good answers can be very short: Fast! Slowly. Together! With a rope.

learn.title: Why? Because …
learn.rule: **Why** asks for a reason. We answer with **Because …**

examples.q: **Why** are Sam and Leo tied together?
examples.a: Because they are in a three-legged race.
Because I want my team to win!
Because it is good for the body.

practice.prompt: ___ is Leo tired? — Because running is hard work.

learn.teacherNote: Why and Because go together. Do not expect long sentences: Because it is fun. is a very good answer.

learn.title: Build a question

examples.from: Mia is running between the trees.
examples.label: is jumps before Mia
Who takes the place of Sam.

learn.teacherNote: The most common mistake is keeping statement order: “Where Leo is jumping?” Use the Change Machine and let pupils move the helper with their hands.

learn.title: Question words with do and does
learn.rule: For every day: question word + **do / does** + who + verb?

examples.a: Because they are fun and good for us!

learn.teacherNote: This connects Week 1 and Week 2: is / are + -ing for now, do / does for every day. The verb after do / does has no -s.

learn.title: Sports and activities
learn.teacherNote: Sing and act out the verbs. Ask pupils for more activities and sort them into do, play and go.

learn.title: Moving: around, through, over, under
learn.rule: A verb + a preposition shows **where someone is moving**.

examples.label: through = in one side, out the other

practice.explain: He is above the hurdles → over.
In one side, out the other → through.

learn.teacherNote: Act them out: walk around a chair, crawl under a table, step over a book. Pupils say the sentence as a friend moves.

learn.title: Moving: up, down, across, past
learn.rule: **up** ↑ **down** ↓ **across** = to the other side. **past** = next to it and on.

examples.label: past = next to it and on

practice.explain: He is not going in. He is going next to it and on → past.

learn.teacherNote: Past is the hardest one. Walk past the teacher’s desk without stopping. Do not confuse it with “past” for time.

learn.title: Moving: into, out of, between
learn.rule: **into** = going in. **out of** = coming out. **between** = with one thing on each side.

examples.text: Sam is stepping **out of** the sandbox.
examples.label: out of → coming out
between = a tree on each side

practice.explain: A tree on each side → between.

learn.teacherNote: Out of is two words. Between needs two things: between the trees, between the cones.

learn.title: Follow the path
learn.rule: Give directions: **Start at … Go over … Run around … Finish at …**

examples.text: **Go up** the ladder and **walk across** the bridge.
**Run between** the trees and **finish** at the gate!

learn.teacherNote: To give directions we use the base verb with no subject: Run around … Make a path in the classroom. One pupil gives directions, a friend follows.

learn.title: Parts of my body
learn.rule: My **heart, lungs, brain, bones** and **muscles** work for me every day.

examples.text: This is my **heart**. It beats faster when I run.
These are my **lungs**. I breathe with them.
This is my **brain**. I think with it.
These are my **bones**. They hold up my body.
These are my **muscles**. They help me move.

practice.prompt: My ___ help me jump and move.

learn.teacherNote: Pupils point to each part on their own body while they say the word.

learn.title: A strong body
learn.rule: Moving your body gives you **energy** and makes you **strong**.

examples.text: After sport, Ana is **relaxed** and happy.
Mia is **breathing hard**. Her lungs are growing strong.
Leo is **tired**. He needs a **short break**.
Mia is writing an **exercise plan**. Move your body for one hour every day!

practice.prompt: Leo is ___. He needs a short break.

learn.teacherNote: Link the new words to the reading in the book. Ask: How do you feel after sport? What gives you energy?

learn.title: Move more every day
learn.rule: Small changes help: **take the stairs, walk to school, dance!**

examples.text: Sam is **playing video games**. His body is not moving much!

examples.a: I can take the stairs and walk to school.

practice.prompt: Which one moves your body more?
practice.explain: The stairs make your body work.

learn.teacherNote: When you listen, look at the speaker and nod. Practise polite listening words in pairs: Uh-huh. Yeah. Right. I understand.

learn.title: Bounce back!
learn.rule: Something is difficult? **Keep trying. Learn. Stay positive. Ask for help.**

examples.text: Ana is **disappointed**. Her serve is not very good.
Leo is **missing** the ball. The other team is winning.
“Sometimes we win and sometimes we lose. That’s OK.”
examples.speaker: Sam and Leo

groups.label: This does not help
words: I am not good at this.

practice.prompt: Sam falls. What can he say?
The game is difficult. What can you do?
practice.explain: Ask for help when you need it.

learn.teacherNote: Talk about a time when something was difficult. Pupils role-play: one wants to quit, the other gives an idea to bounce back.
